h1: The 4 Best 40V Leaf Blowers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: four Greenworks 40V cordless leaf blowers, from 135 CFM sweepers to a 730 CFM yard clearer, with picks by yard size.
summary: The 730 CFM Greenworks 40V is our best overall pick for clearing a full yard of wet leaves. The 550 CFM and 500 CFM Greenworks models are the middle ground for average lots, and the 135 CFM model is only for patios and light debris. Only Greenworks models state a 40V platform in the facts we reviewed, so this ranking covers four of them.
intro: The biggest mistake with a leaf blower is trusting the voltage badge and ignoring airflow. A 40V platform tells you which battery fits, not how much wind you get, and the CFM gap between two blowers on the same battery can be more than fivefold.

We reviewed the Greenworks 40V blowers whose listings name the platform and an airflow number. We ranked them on CFM, then on how well each size suits a real yard, and we left out blowers whose listings do not confirm 40V.

products.name: Greenworks 40V Electric Leaf Blower
products.verdict: The strongest 40V airflow in this group at 730 CFM.
products.description:
This Greenworks 40V cordless blower is rated at 730 CFM, the highest airflow of the four. It sits in the $200 to $500 price bucket.

It ranks first because airflow is what clears wet and matted leaves. The tradeoff against the 550 CFM model below is cost: you pay a full tier more for about a third more wind.

Choose it for a large yard with heavy leaf fall. Skip it if your yard is small, since a cheaper model will do the same job.
products.idealFor: Large yards with heavy leaf fall.
products.skipIf: You only clear a patio or small lawn.

products.name: Greenworks 40V Electric Leaf Blower (550 CFM)
products.verdict: A balanced 550 CFM blower for an average suburban lot.
products.description:
This model is rated at 550 CFM and runs cordless on the 40V platform, in the $100 to $200 bucket.

Second place goes to it since it delivers you most of the airflow of the top pick at roughly half the price tier. It trails the 730 CFM model on stubborn wet leaves.

Buy it for a typical yard. Skip it if you have a lot of heavy, damp leaf cover.
products.skipIf: You face heavy, wet leaf cover.

products.name: Greenworks 40V Cordless Leaf Blower (500 CFM)
products.verdict: Just under the 550 CFM model, at the same price tier.
products.description:
This cordless 40V blower is rated at 500 CFM and sits in the $100 to $200 range.

Third place goes here since it offers 50 CFM less than the model above in the same tier. The gap is small, so it makes sense mainly if it is cheaper on the day you buy.

It suits small to mid-size lawns. Skip it if you can pick up the 550 CFM version for the same money.
products.skipIf: The 550 CFM model costs the same.

products.name: Greenworks 40V Cordless Leaf Blower (135 CFM)
products.verdict: A light-duty 135 CFM sweeper for patios and driveways.
products.description:
This cordless 40V model is rated at only 135 CFM, in the $100 to $200 bucket.

Last place is earned as its airflow is a fraction of the others, which limits it to dry leaves and dust. It costs a similar tier to stronger models.

Buy it for a patio, deck or walkway. Skip it for real lawn leaf clearing.
products.skipIf: You need to clear a lawn of leaves.

whatMatters.detail: CFM is the volume of air the blower moves each minute. It matters because higher volume shifts wet and heavy leaves. Look for the CFM number in the listing title or bullets, not just the word powerful.
A 40V label means the blower uses that voltage of battery pack. It matters because matching packs can be shared across other tools. Check the listing states 40V and whether the battery is included.
A cordless blower removes the extension lead and lets you reach far corners. The tradeoff is a limited run time. Look for a power type line saying cordless.
A bigger yard needs more airflow and run time. Small patios do not. Compare the CFM against the area you clear and size up if you have heavy leaf fall.
Price rises with airflow, but not evenly. Compare each bucket against the CFM figure to see where the extra money goes.

cards.text: Moves wet, matted leaves and large areas. The 730 CFM, 550 CFM and 500 CFM Greenworks models do this.

cards.label: Light duty
cards.text: Clears dust and dry leaves from hard surfaces. The 135 CFM Greenworks model fits here.

howToChoose.note: Most buyers should default to 550 CFM or higher.

faq.a: Not directly. Voltage defines the battery platform, while CFM measures airflow. Compare the CFM number between models.
Check each listing. Some bundles include the battery and charger, and bare tools do not.

faq.q: Is the 730 CFM Greenworks worth it over the 550 CFM?
faq.a: Only for large yards or wet leaves. Most average lawns are handled by 550 CFM in a lower price tier.

faq.q: How do I get the most from a cordless blower?
faq.a: Work with the wind and sweep leaves into piles in one direction. Fully charge the battery before a large job.
Clear debris from the intake and nozzle after use, and store the battery indoors away from extreme heat or cold.

faq.q: Is the 135 CFM model enough for a lawn?
faq.a: It is too weak for most lawn clearing. Keep it for patios, decks and walkways.

finalTake: The 730 CFM Greenworks 40V is the best here for big yards, and the 550 CFM model is the sensible buy for most homes. Use the 500 CFM version if it costs less, and treat the 135 CFM model as a patio tool. Always check that the battery is included before you order.
